data.name: filterColumnInRangeAddBtn.SuperTip
data.value: Click below the header you want to filter. A range picker will appear. Select the range to be added to excluded from the column values, and click OK. (Works for tables and pivots, but it may be slower for pivots. Avoid applying many filters to large data pivots or save open workbooks before use.)

data.name: filterColumnNotInRangeBtn.SuperTip
data.value: Click below the header you want to filter. A range picker will appear. Select the range to be excluded from the column values, and click OK. (Works for tables and pivots, but it may be slower for pivots. Avoid applying many filters to large data pivots or save open workbooks before use.)

data.name: filterColumnNotInRangeAddBtn.SuperTip
data.value: Click below the header you want to filter. A range picker will appear. Select the range to be extra excluded from the column values, and click OK. (Works for tables and pivots, but it may be slower for pivots. Avoid applying many filters to large data pivots or save open workbooks before use.)

data.name: filterColumnFromRangeInRangeButton.SuperTip
data.value: Click below the header you want to filter, and a range picker will appear. Pick the range you want to use for filtering, and click OK (Works for tables and pivots, but it may be slower for pivots. Avoid applying many filters to large data pivots or save open workbooks before use.)

data.name: filterColumnFromRangeNotInRangeButton.SuperTip
data.value: Click below the header you want to filter, and a range picker will appear. Pick the range you want to use for filtering that will be excluded from the column values, and click OK (Works for tables and pivots, but it may be slower for pivots. Avoid applying many filters to large data pivots or save open workbooks before use.)

data.name: filterColumnInRegexButton.SuperTip
data.value: Click below the header you want to filter. An input box will appear. Enter a Regular Expression (Regex) pattern you want to use for filtering, and click OK. (Works for tables and pivots, but it may be slower for pivots. Avoid applying many filters to large data pivots or save open workbooks before use.)

data.name: filterColumnInRegexAddButton.SuperTip
data.value: Click below the header you want to filter. An input box will appear. Enter a Regular Expression (Regex) pattern you want to use for extra filtering, and click OK. (Works for tables and pivots, but it may be slower for pivots. Avoid applying many filters to large data pivots or save open workbooks before use.)

data.name: filterColumnNotInRegexButton.SuperTip
data.value: Click below the header you want to filter. An input box will appear. Enter a Regular Expression (Regex) pattern you want to use for filtering out, it will exclude matching values from a filter, and click OK. (Works for tables and pivots, but it may be slower for pivots. Avoid applying many filters to large data pivots or save open workbooks before use.)

data.name: filterColumnNotInRegexAddButton.SuperTip
data.value: Click below the header you want to filter. An input box will appear. Enter a Regular Expression (Regex) pattern you want to use for extra filtering out, and click OK. (Works for tables and pivots, but it may be slower for pivots. Avoid applying many filters to large data pivots or save open workbooks before use.)

data.name: filterColumnFlipFilterBtn.SuperTip
data.value: Click below the header you want to flip the filter and click the button (Works for tables and pivots, but it may be slower for pivots. Avoid applying many filters to large data pivots or save open workbooks before use.)

data.name: filterColumnSplitButton.SuperTip
data.value: Click below the header you want to filter. A range picker will appear. Select the range you want to use for filtering, and click OK (Works for tables and pivots, but it may be slower for pivots. Avoid applying many filters to large data pivots or save open workbooks before use.)

data.name: formatTrueFalseButton.SuperTip
data.value: Select a rectangular range, and it will apply conditional formatting for TRUE and FALSE values. It will also add functionality to double-click cells with TRUE or FALSE to toggle their values (formula will be replaced with a value after toggle).

data.name: saveSelectedWorksheetsAsTxtButton.SuperTip
data.value: Saves selected worksheets from the workbook to separate tab delimited txt files. It will show a dialog where to save them. If any cell contains a tab or a new line it will warn about it and offer to remove it by inserting a space if between words.

data.name: saveAllWorksheetsAsTxtButton.SuperTip
data.value: Saves all worksheets from the workbook to separate tab delimited txt files. It will show a dialog where to save them. If any cell contains a tab or a new line it will warn about it and offer to remove it by inserting a space if between words.

data.name: runCustomFormButton.SuperTip
data.value: Lists macros that begin with a custom phrase and allow you to run them. (To use this feature, enable "Trust access to the VBA project object model" in Excel Trust Center settings and define custom phrase in XML FormsMacrosSearchKeys.xml under "RunCustom". File is inside "Properties Files" folder.) (To close the form, press Esc or right-click on it.)

data.name: runPvTemplateBtn.SuperTip
data.value: Opens a form that searches for all pivot templates starting with "CreatePvForm", which can be run by double-clicking. (To use this feature, enable "Trust access to the VBA project object model" in Excel Trust Center settings.) (To close the form, press Esc or right-click on it.)

data.name: runS4ExtractButton.SuperTip
data.value: Opens a form to execute predefined SAP exports, often based on the selected range values. You can double-click to run macros starting with "LoginToS4AndGet." (To use this feature, enable SAP scripting, trust all save paths without warnings, and enable "Trust access to the VBA project object model" in Excel Trust Center settings.) (To close the form, press Esc or right-click on it.)

data.name: browserButton.SuperTip
data.value: Launches an Edge-powered browser in a form. Choose a website, and if auto-import is checked, it can import any Excel file (first sheet) or txt/csv file into your active workbook. (Keep the browser open to avoid logging in each time.)

data.name: updateMacrosButton.SuperTip
data.value: Opens a file picker for selecting Excel VBA modules (.bas) or custom (.macro) update files. Then, another picker opens to select the workbook for updating. It will add new macros to the chosen macro workbook or update existing ones. If your module contains extra macros not present in the new version, these macros will be retained when updating the entire module. You can update only one workbook at a time, and it is best not to mix entire modules and individual macros to avoid conflicts. (To use this feature, enable "Trust access to the VBA project object model" in Excel Trust Center settings.)
